evidence.field: 三部 entry; PDF p. 25, printed p. 13; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0025/source.png, crop bounds x=1900–2900, y=1750–3750 (3000×4095 source)
evidence.text: Directly inspected the scan pixels. Under the visible headword 三, 白于蓝 describes it as 指事字 and identifies the original sense as the numeral three (“二加一为三”). The passage cites 《庄子·齐物论》, 《广韵·谈韵》, and other received texts for ordinal use and extended use referring broadly to multiplicity. It says the graph used three horizontal strokes to represent quantity; Warring States forms sometimes add 戈 or 弋, and the 弋-added form continued into Han. It distinguishes oracle-bone 三, whose three strokes are equal, from 气, whose middle stroke is shorter. The headword, diagram, paragraph, and paragraph end are visible on this page; page 26 starts with 王 and 皇 entries, not a continuation of 三.

evidence.field: §2.1.1, 商朝数词{三}的用字; cited oracle-bone corpus records H.16189 and H.37453
evidence.text: The article reports 三 used for the numeral in two 《甲骨文合集》 examples and says its survey found one graph slot for the numeral in Shang sources. This corroborates the book's account of early numeral use, but the article gives no precise inscription year or reign, and this researcher did not inspect the cited artifact facsimiles.

evidence.source: Wu Yuanyuan, Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research
evidence.text: The author argues that the numeral sense is the original sense: oracle-bone 三 has three strokes and is used for the number in cited examples, while the surveyed oracle-bone evidence shows no use for Xu Shen's gloss 天地人之道. This is the author's evidence-based argument and conclusion; it does not turn the received Shuowen gloss into a false quotation, but distinguishes it from the proposed original numeral sense.
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（四）

evidence.source: Academia Sinica Institute of History and Philology, International Computer Chinese Characters and Variant Forms Knowledgebase
evidence.text: The entry lists a bronze record 集成04261, Chu manuscript forms, and a Small Seal form. It interprets the three equal horizontal strokes as three equal counting rods representing three. This supports reporting the counting-rod explanation as a paleographic interpretation, not as demonstrated proof that the earliest graph was directly copied from physical rods.

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》 transcription with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.field: 三 entry, lines 8, 12–16; later commentary lines 22–27
evidence.text: The transmitted text says “天地人之道也。从三數” and records “古文三从弋” for 弎. Duan Yucai distinguishes the gloss from the graphic explanation and relates the strokes to the three powers. This is a received lexicographic interpretation, not an independent Shang-period attestation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「三」

evidence.source: 袁倫強, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心
evidence.field: 《新甲骨文編》（增訂本）校勘劄記, section 2 三, discussing 合22600 and examples 合33060、35168、35180
evidence.text: The author corrects an oracle-bone graph catalogued as 三 to 气, describing the graphic distinction as equal-length strokes for 三 versus a shorter middle stroke for 气, while noting that 气 was sometimes carved in a form resembling 三. This independently supports the distinction reported in 字源 and cautions that isolated graph shape can be ambiguous; context and occurrence identity matter.
evidence.title: 袁倫強：《新甲骨文編》（增訂本）校勘劄記

evidence.source: Wu Yuanyuan, Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research
evidence.text: The survey reports 三 as the only graph slot it found for numeral three in Shang sources; 參 appears additionally in Zhou-period sources; 品/晶 appears among reported Spring-and-Autumn/Warring-States Chu manuscript evidence; and excavated Qin-Han sources in the survey contain 三 and 參. These are alternate written graphs for the same numeral, not a demonstrated graphic descent of 三 from those forms. The author treats a single transmitted Hanshu 叄 example as possibly later substitution and excludes it from her Qin-Han count.
evidence.kind: scholarly corpus survey with qualified textual assessment

gaps: No artifact facsimile for the book's labeled Shang or Western Zhou specimens was independently inspected; the scan is a printed scholarly account and specimen diagram. The Shang examples H.16189 and H.37453 are survey-reported without precise year or reign.

The source describes ordinal and multiplicity uses with transmitted textual examples, but this research did not establish a complete dated chronology for the spoken numeral's semantic extensions. Keep those as attributed examples, not as a dated sequence inferred from glosses.
The Academy Sinica counting-rod interpretation is a paleographic proposal. Direct derivation of the earliest graph from physical rods is not established by inspected evidence.

The Baxter–Sagart structured dataset is not present in this checkout at sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, so the supplied dossier's historical reading row could not be independently checked against that exact local table in this invocation. No sound component is proposed for 三.
No source here establishes a direct graphic transition from 弎 to 三; the sources attest 弎 as an ancient/variant form and describe its structure, but not a linear descent.
